findings.highlight: don't go running off to cover it.
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩とか編集長に押し付けてでも帰ってくるんだよ？
findings.explanation: Setsuna orders Haruki to come home even if he has to dump a late scoop on his seniors or editor-in-chief. Todokanai TL drops that absolute and professionally outrageous condition, leaves the quotation open, and weakens the exact promise the emergency will test.
findings.japanese:
「夜遅く特ダネが入って来ても
取材に行っちゃ駄目だからね？
先輩とか編集長に押し付けてでも帰ってくるんだよ？」
findings.todokanai: "Even if some special scoop pops up late tonight, don't go running off to cover it.

findings.highlight: The second time is during my birthday in April.
findings.evidenceJa: 別に、俺としてはどうということもないただの日だけど、多分、一年で一番のご馳走が用意されているのはこの日だ。
findings.explanation: Haruki calls his own birthday an ordinary day to him, while noting that Setsuna probably prepares the year's greatest feast for it. Todokanai TL omits both his self-effacement and her lavish care, reducing the second annual occasion to a date on a list.
findings.japanese:
二つめは、４月の俺の誕生日。
別に、俺としてはどうということもないただの日だけど、
多分、一年で一番のご馳走が用意されているのはこの日だ。
findings.todokanai: The second time is during my birthday in April.

findings.highlight: the day we faced our greatest crisis at a seaside hotel;
findings.evidenceJa: 欧州の小都市で、ふたたびすれ違いが始まってしまったり。
findings.explanation: The Christmas Eve history has a third episode: in a small European city the couple began missing each other again. Todokanai TL cuts the list after the seaside hotel and leaves the sentence on a semicolon, erasing the later repetition that makes the date an enduring cycle rather than two old incidents.
findings.japanese:
北の温泉で、永遠の友情を誓ったり、
海沿いのホテルで、決定的な危機を迎えたり、
欧州の小都市で、ふたたびすれ違いが始まってしまったり。
findings.todokanai: It's the day we once swore eternal friendship in a hot spring up north; the day we faced our greatest crisis at a seaside hotel;

findings.highlight: If I'm to keep my promise with Setsuna to see her before 10 PM, I'll have to finish things up rather quickly.
findings.evidenceJa:
雪菜と約束した『２２時までに自宅』を守るには、
そろそろ仕事を収束させていかなくちゃならない時間帯だ。
findings.explanation: The promise is specifically to be home by 22:00, not merely to see Setsuna before ten — The deadline still governs his attempt to leave.
findings.japanese:
雪菜と約束した『２２時までに自宅』を守るには、
そろそろ仕事を収束させていかなくちゃならない時間帯だ。
findings.todokanai: If I'm to keep my promise with Setsuna to see her before 10 PM, I'll have to finish things up rather quickly.

findings.highlight: my two seniors seem to have a lot going on during Christmas Eve…
findings.evidenceJa: 今年のクリスマスはどうやら色々とある……というか、今年に関しては色々とないみたいだった。
findings.explanation: Haruki starts to say the seniors have various things going on, then corrects himself: this year they conspicuously have nothing going on. Todokanai TL cuts before the reversal and states the rejected positive premise, obscuring why both resent his married Christmas.
findings.japanese:
……なのだが、二人の先輩方は、
今年のクリスマスはどうやら色々とある……というか、
今年に関しては色々とないみたいだった。
findings.todokanai: …Is what I'd like to say, but my two seniors seem to have a lot going on during Christmas Eve…

findings.highlight: She's famous in the industry as the public relations beauty of Knights Records.
findings.evidenceJa: なんでこんな堅物に引っかかっちゃったかなぁ
findings.explanation: Suzuki wonders how a famous beauty like Setsuna ever got caught by such a stiff, straitlaced man. Todokanai TL omits the insult and leaves the quote open, so Matsuoka's sexual answer that Haruki was probably 'stiff in various ways' loses the word it is punning on.
findings.japanese:
「ちょっと洒落になんないもんね～北原君の奥さん。
ナイツレコードの美人広報って業界でも有名なんだよね？
なんでこんな堅物に引っかかっちゃったかなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "Your wife is something else, isn't she? She's famous in the industry as the public relations beauty of Knights Records.

findings.highlight: why don't you just go home?
findings.evidenceJa: だいたい松岡さんだって彼女との約束ないんですか？
findings.explanation: Haruki specifically asks whether Matsuoka has plans with his girlfriend. Todokanai TL drops the question and leaves the quotation open, so Matsuoka's 'That's precisely the thing' has no translated referent.
findings.japanese:
「……二人とも、そんな無駄話してる暇があったら、
さっさと帰ったらどうですか？
だいたい松岡さんだって彼女との約束ないんですか？」
findings.todokanai: "…You two, if you can afford to waste time rambling on like that, why don't you just go home?

findings.highlight: if you're going to be in a long-term relationship,
findings.evidenceJa: 断り続けて悪印象持たれるのも……
findings.explanation: Haruki advises visiting because the relationship may continue and repeatedly refusing would make a bad impression on her family. Todokanai TL cuts the conditional advice mid-clause, omits the concrete social consequence, and leaves the quotation unfinished.
findings.japanese:
「いや、実家くらい行けばいいでしょう。
もしかしたら、ずっと付き合っていくかもしれないし、
断り続けて悪印象持たれるのも……」
findings.todokanai: "No, I don't see the problem with visiting her family. Besides, if you're going to be in a long-term relationship,

findings.highlight: half-baked men like this are a dime a dozen.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はまだ自分に自信が持てないんだ～とか、けど、決してお前に飽きたわけじゃないんだ～とか
findings.explanation: Suzuki quotes the stock excuses of an indecisive man—he still lacks confidence, but definitely has not tired of his girlfriend. Todokanai TL omits both quoted lines, so Matsuoka's next suspicion that she has bugged him loses the uncannily exact words it answers.
findings.japanese:
「……あ～いるいるこういう煮え切らない男。
俺はまだ自分に自信が持てないんだ～とか、
けど、決してお前に飽きたわけじゃないんだ～とか」
findings.todokanai: "…Oh dear, half-baked men like this are a dime a dozen.

findings.highlight: Since you two have all this time to sit around chit-chatting,
findings.evidenceJa: 今年いっぱい、一度も家に帰れないくらいの仕事あげようか？
findings.explanation: Suzuki threatens to give both men enough work that they will not make it home once for the rest of the year. Todokanai TL drops the entire threat and leaves the line on a comma, removing the immediate cause of their panicked refusals and attempted escape.
findings.japanese:
「……二人とも、こんな無駄話してる暇があったら、
今年いっぱい、一度も家に帰れないくらいの
仕事あげようか？」
findings.todokanai: "…Since you two have all this time to sit around chit-chatting,

findings.evidenceJa: 大事な用があって絶対に帰らなくちゃならないときに限って、狙ったように新しい仕事が舞い込んできて
findings.explanation: Matsuoka defines his 'law': precisely when he has important plans and absolutely must leave, new work arrives as though aiming for him. Todokanai TL omits the entire rule after its generic opening, leaving no explanation of the named law that the ensuing ministerial scoop fulfills.
findings.japanese:
「俺、いっつもそうなんだよ。大事な用があって
絶対に帰らなくちゃならないときに限って、
狙ったように新しい仕事が舞い込んできて……」

findings.evidenceJa: 日付をまたぐ、その瞬間だった。
findings.explanation: Haruki reaches Setsuna at the exact instant the date crosses midnight, too late to keep the Christmas Eve promise; the next sentence marks the day vanishing. 'Nearly at midnight' places the call before the deadline and contradicts that symbolic loss.
findings.japanese:
目の回る忙しさがほんの一段落つき、
やっと雪菜への連絡が取れたのは、
日付をまたぐ、その瞬間だった。
findings.todokanai: It was only after the bustle had settled down a bit that I was able to get in touch with Setsuna, nearly at midnight.

findings.highlight: The moment I was about to give up, an exasperated voice reached me from the receiver.
findings.evidenceJa:
と、途方に暮れそうになったその瞬間、
電話口から、ようやく待ち焦がれた声が聞こえてきた。
findings.explanation: The voice is one Haruki has longed desperately to hear; 'an exasperated voice' adds an emotional judgment before her words — His relief and her dry response remain.
findings.japanese:
と、途方に暮れそうになったその瞬間、
電話口から、ようやく待ち焦がれた声が聞こえてきた。
findings.todokanai: The moment I was about to give up, an exasperated voice reached me from the receiver.

findings.explanation: Haruki says 'So it really was work,' registering surprise and relief; 'Were you really at work?' sounds like a continuing accusation — His next line explains the charitable lie he had imagined.

findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちの絆が弱く、脆く、お互いに、間違った気遣いをしてしまっていたあの頃。
findings.explanation: The line defines the past as a time when their bond was weak and fragile and both practiced mistaken forms of consideration. Todokanai TL retains only 'long ago,' omitting the diagnosis that the following lies, vows, and corrected marriage are structured against.
findings.japanese:
ずっとずっと昔……
俺たちの絆が弱く、脆く、
お互いに、間違った気遣いをしてしまっていたあの頃。

findings.highlight: Nothing happens. We remain ourselves, just like we swore to… No, it's more like something that kind of just happened on its own.
findings.evidenceJa:
やっぱり、俺たちは俺たちのままだって、
そんなふうに誓いあい……いや、適当に決めあった。
findings.explanation: They loosely agreed that even after a broken promise they remain themselves; 'something that kind of just happened on its own' removes their mutual decision — The resilient-marriage principle is still stated.
findings.japanese:
やっぱり、俺たちは俺たちのままだって、
そんなふうに誓いあい……いや、適当に決めあった。
findings.todokanai: Nothing happens. We remain ourselves, just like we swore to… No, it's more like something that kind of just happened on its own.
